Q: How does code get executed in embedded systems? A:

I get the impression you're most interested in what sybreon calls "step 2." Lots can happen there, and it varies greatly by platform. Usually, this stuff is handled by some combination of bootloader, board support package, C runtime (CRT), and if you've got one, the OS.

Typically, after the reset vector, some sort of bootloader will execute from flash. This bootloader might just set up hardware and jump into your application's CRT, also in flash. In this case, the CRT would probably clear the .bss, copy the .data to RAM, etc. In other systems, the bootloader can scatter-load the application from a coded file, like an ELF, and the CRT just sets up other runtime stuff (heap, etc.). All of this happens before the CRT calls the application's main().

If your application is statically linked, linker directives will specify the addresses where .data/.bss and stack are initialized. These values are either linked into the CRT or coded into the ELF. In a dynamically-linked environment, application loading is usually handled by an OS which re-targets the ELF to run in whatever memory the OS designates.

Also, some targets run applications from flash, but others will copy the executable .text from flash to RAM. (This is usually a speed/footprint tradeoff, since RAM is faster/wider than flash on most targets.)

Q: Update during resize in Pygame A:

I updated sloth's code:

  1. Keeps running while moving the window
  2. Get pygame's hwnd directly rather than depend on GetForegroundWindow()
  3. Removed unneeded code (lambda, DOUBLEBUF, RedrawWindow, VIDEORESIZE)
  4. Added a moving box to see the program keeps running while moving/resizing
  5. Added clock for consistent framerate
import pygame, sys, win32gui, win32con

def wndProc(hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam):
    if uMsg in (win32con.WM_SIZE, win32con.WM_MOVE, win32con.WM_SYSCOMMAND, win32con.WM_TIMER): mainloop()
    return win32gui.CallWindowProc(oldWndProc, hWnd, uMsg, wParam, lParam)

pos = 0
def update():
    global pos
    pos+=1
    if pos>screen.get_width(): pos = -100 # loop back to left of screen

def mainloop(): # draw and update
    dt = fpsclock.tick(60) # limit fps (resizing events will try draw a lot. this will slow it down)
    screen.fill((150,210,240)) # blue background
    pygame.draw.rect(screen, (255,255,255), (pos,20,100,60)) # white cloud floating
    pygame.display.flip()
    update()

def main():
    global screen, fpsclock, oldWndProc # simplest to make screen info global
    pygame.init()
    screen = pygame.display.set_mode((800,400), pygame.RESIZABLE)
    pygame.display.set_caption("Live Resizable Window")
    fpsclock = pygame.time.Clock()
    oldWndProc = win32gui.SetWindowLong(pygame.display.get_wm_info()["window"], win32con.GWL_WNDPROC, wndProc)

    while True:
        for event in pygame.event.get():
            if event.type == pygame.QUIT: pygame.quit(); sys.exit()
            elif event.type == pygame.KEYDOWN:
                if event.key == pygame.K_ESCAPE: pygame.quit(); sys.exit()
        mainloop()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Q: My discord bot isn't responding to my commands A:

If you copy it from somewhere else, they probably don't do it right (proof: here and here). After checking the docs (to check is my guess is right), it's await message.channel.send('things'), not await message.send('Hello!'). So to fix it, change to this:

import discord

client = discord.Client()

@client.event
async def on_ready():
    print('We have logged in as {0.user}'.format(client))

@client.event
async def on_message(message):
    if message.author == client.user:
        return

    if message.content.startswith('$hello'):
        await message.channel.send('Hello!')

client.run('MY TOKEN IS HERE')

PS: Because you only show the copied code, I only answer that code

Q: How to use a Puppet File Resource to give different permissions on a directory than to it's files? A:

If you only need this for a static set of individual directories:

  1. Ensure the pluginsync setting is true. This was an issue when you first asked your question, meanwhile this is by default enabled (true).
  2. Create a custom fact my_module/lib/facter/php_sessions.rb: 
    Facter.add('php_sessions') do
    setcode do
        Dir.children('/var/phpsessions')
    end
end
    I’m no Ruby expert. Dir.children includes directories, so adjust it if /var/phpsessions contains directories, too, which you do not want to alter.
  3. Use the fact. 
    file {
    default:
        group  => 'admin',
    ;
    'phpsessions_directory':
        path   => '/var/phpsessions',
        ensure => directory,
        owner  => 'root',
        mode   => 'ug=rwx,o=',
    ;
    $facts.get('php_sessions'):
        ensure => file,
        owner  => 'apache',
        mode   => 'u=rw,go=',
    ;
}

If you need this for a dynamic set of directories:

  • This is not possible with file resources. Perhaps some module available via Forge.Puppet.com provides a custom resource type meeting your requirements nonetheless.
  • The directories can still be managed via a file resource. For the files, however, you need take the exec detour. An incomplete manifest just to showcase the principle for the file mode. 
    $directories = file {
    default:
        ensure => directory,
    ;
    'foo_deconfiguration':
        path   => '/foo',
    ;
    'xyz_landfill':
        path   => '/xyz',
    ;
}

$change_mode_0600 = @(EOT/L)
    find . \
        -type f \
        ! -path './*/*' \
        ! -perm 0600 \
        -exec chmod 0600 '{}' +
    |- EOT

$directories.each { |$dir|
    exec {
        "change_${dir[path]}_mode":
            command => $change_mode_0600,
            cwd     => $dir['path'],
        ;
    }
}
    Provision of find is mandatory for all POSIX™‐compliant systems. The ! ‑path './*/*' predicate excludes files in sub‐directories. Proceed with the file owner by analogy.

Notes:

  • Parent directories are “auto‐required”. It is not wrong, but unnecessary to indicate a require relationship.
  • The php_sessions fact is evaluated on all clients in the environment the module is in. You may want to check whether the /var/phpsessions directory exists beforehand.
  • If supported by the underlying file system, another method for your particular situation might be to define an inherited NFSv4 ACL rule. POSIX.1e ACLs have some inheritance, too.

Q: How can I extract rows of information from multiple sheets by typing in a date A:

Advanced filter (AF) would be one way to do this. It does require a small bit of manual work, however, and the data would all be on one sheet.

This example assumes your data starts in column A on a sheet named Sheet1 with the headers running from A1:K1 (based on information from your question).

1- Name your input range Database like this:

=OFFSET(Sheet1!$A$1,0,0,11,COUNTA(Sheet1!$A:$A))

This will ensure that each time you run AF, it will always pick up the latest data added to the bottom of the existing list.

2- Copy the headers from the data sheet to other columns in the same sheet. Copy only the headers. Ex: if your columns spanned from A1:K1, copy A1:K1 to M1:W1.
3- Hide columns N through W.
4- In cell M2, put the date you want to search for.
5- See below for filter criteria.

Example:

Columns A through K have sample meter data:

Columns M through W contain the criteria range, with columns N through W hidden:

In cell M2, put the date you want to return values for:

Go to Data » Filter » Advanced Filter (or however you do it in your version of Excel, mine is 2003) and use the following criteria:

  • List Range should always be Database to capture any new records that may have been added since the last time AF was run.
  • Criteria Range should always be $M$1:$W$2 although you can put this anywhere and even name it if you prefer.
  • Copy to should be wherever you want to place the matching records, however it must be on the same sheet (sorry, I did say this was only one possible solution)

When you click 'OK' you should see the matching records for that date put into columns Z:AJ. Change the date and go to Data » Filter » Advanced Filter again to filter records based on the new date. If you add new records you should see them in the filter because we used a dynamic range name (Database) to grab them.

HTH

Q: The server principal is not able to access the database under the current security context in SQL Server A:

Check the permissions in the user's properties in your SQL environment (via SQL Server Management Studio or similar tool) to see if your user is correctly mapped to the database you are trying to log into.

Note that the user may be trying to access a View, a Trigger, or Stored Procedure which makes calls to other databases where they are not authorized.
